subject: Dedicated capacity: performance validation & GPU comparison follow-up
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@cloudpay.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra+eng@cloudpay.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery — performance targets and Dedicated ask

Thanks again for the call earlier, Marcus. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying points so we can align the validation run: 

- Target user-visible SLO: 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for short-form responses (avg 30 tokens) and <= 600ms for longer multi-turn responses (avg 150 tokens).
- Throughput shape: steady-state baseline of ~200 QPS for small inference requests, with bursts up to 800 QPS during peak payroll batch windows (~6–9 minutes).
- Concurrency/streams: our streaming integration expects ~150 concurrent live streaming sessions (token-by-token), each averaging 8 tokens/sec. We need streaming P95 <= 300ms per chunk.
- Data plane constraint: payloads include structured payment metadata (~1–2KB) and must not be retained by vendor.

As discussed, we'd like a focused Dedicated capacity validation that compares H100 vs A100 equivalent configs and gives a recommended reserved throughput, plus a cost estimate for a three-month pilot. We can provide a realistic traffic replay (sample payloads attached) and we prefer the run next week (Mon/Tue).

Next steps from CloudPay: we can confirm the replay dataset and block out a 3-hour window for a stress+soak run.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform
CloudPay AI

Hi Elaine — great call, and thanks for the clear targets. I pulled together a short test plan and initial sizing notes (attached). High level response below and proposed next steps: 

Summary of what we'll validate during the Dedicated run:
- Latency validation: P95 tail testing for short (30-token) and long (150-token) responses under steady and burst traffic.
- Streaming validation: token-chunk latency and head-of-line behavior for 150 concurrent streaming sessions.
- GPU comparison: H100 (80GB) vs A100 (80GB) with bf16 and int8 quantization profiles where supported.
- Reserved throughput recommendation: we will produce a recommended reserved throughput (tokens/sec) and translate to number of GPUs for a 99.9% of windows pass rate.

Immediate asks from Redwood:
1) Confirm a 3-hour window and preferred date (we have Mon 12/07 or Tue 12/08 open).
2) Send replay payloads (you attached a sample; full set would be great).
3) Any hard constraints on encryption/KMS or egress (we support customer-managed KMS on Private, request for Dedicated noted).

I've attached "redwood_proposed_test_plan.pdf" — it includes the metrics we'll collect, the gating criteria, and a short checklist for the run. If that looks good I'll schedule internal capacity and loop in our infra team.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 14:12:00 -08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: CloudPay validation — preliminary sizing thoughts

Monica / Ben — internal note after the discovery call and before we lock schedule. High-level recommendations and risks: 

1) Workload profile summary (per CloudPay): baseline ~200 QPS small tokens, bursts to 800 QPS, 150 concurrent streaming sessions @ ~8 tps.
2) GPU tradeoffs: H100 will give ~1.6–2x inference throughput for the transformer sizes they described vs A100 at similar latency targets; however, H100 costs ~1.7x on our procurement. Int8 delivers better cost-efficiency but only for model variants we can quantize losslessly — need to confirm model family.
3) Reserved throughput estimation (very early): to hit steady-state baseline + buffer and meet P95 <=250ms for short responses, I estimate ~3 H100s or ~5 A100s (with optimized batching and KV cache). For peak burst handling without queuing we should consider burst capacity (hot spare GPU or autoscale bump) that can add another ~2 H100s equivalent.
4) Streaming: main risk is head-of-line blocking when mixing many small streaming sessions with batched non-streaming requests. We should validate our dynamic routing (stream lanes) and measure chunk latency with the replay.

Action items for internal ops: Ben — can you validate whether we have 3 H100s free on Dedicated pool for Mon/Tue and estimate incremental cost for an additional 2 H100-equivalents as burst? Monica — please prepare a short canary/rollback plan and the cost delta for H100 vs A100 for a 3-month pilot (include estimated token costs + reserved capacity).

Thanks — Marcus

(Internal only)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 17:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: CloudPay validation — preliminary sizing thoughts

Saw Marcus' note — quick updates from infra: 
- We can provision 3x H100s in the Dedicated sandbox for Mon 12/07 09:00–12:00 PT.
- For burst capacity we can schedule an autoscale window that adds capacity equivalent to ~2 H100s for 20 minutes during the run; estimated incremental infra cost ~USD 7,500 for the test window.
- Canary plan: we'll run a 30-minute low-traffic dry run, then ramp to full replay. If P95 for short responses exceeds 350ms during dry run, we abort and capture logs. Rollback is a switch back to the customer's current hosted model endpoint.

I'll mark resources tentative and share an infra runbook after Marcus confirms schedule.

—Ben
